fields.title: Audit copy-prone workarounds and stale consumer patterns

fields.description: Audit of 7cc8c82e: runlimit/runlimit-core/src/observation.rs:410-411 and attempts.rs:262-265 discard catch_unwind results. Dropping the caught Box<dyn Any + Send> runs application payload destructors outside containment. A callback using panic_any(Payload) where Payload::drop panics makes both helpers unwind. Both helpers are used by memory and PostgreSQL backends after state changes; the observer contract says telemetry cannot change admission results. This is a copy-prone catch-and-ignore pattern, not a default panic-hook concern. Two independent external characterization tests ran on Rust 1.100.0/macOS arm64 and confirmed an outer catch_unwind receives Err from each helper. Keep the fix native to Runlimit; do not add a dependency on Batter. Assess payload disposal rather than adding one more catch that can itself discard an arbitrary payload.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Both observer helpers contain payload destruction; string and custom payload cases are tested, including post-mutation backend behavior; document disposal and runtime limits; preserve dependency direction and run required verification.
fields.title: Contain Runlimit observer panic-payload destruction

fields.description: Audit of 7cc8c82e: worker_binary.rs:73, producer_worker/worker.rs:58, runtime crate docs and Runledger README use RuntimeShutdownSignal::ctrl_c(). shutdown_signal.rs:143-146 only wraps tokio::signal::ctrl_c, whose pinned Unix source registers SignalKind::interrupt. No SIGTERM listener exists in the native examples. A deployed copy receiving SIGTERM therefore bypasses the illustrated report classification and awaited pool closure. This is source-confirmed; no new SIGTERM subprocess experiment was run. Prefer a native library-owned SIGINT/SIGTERM signal constructor and adopt it in worker entrypoints; preserve application-installed signal policy and native ownership.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Native worker examples and quick-start handle SIGINT and SIGTERM through accounted shutdown; subprocess tests prove classification and cleanup; setup errors retained; Unix-only; public API review and docs synchronized.
fields.title: Give native worker examples a Unix termination signal path

fields.description: Audit of 7cc8c82e: runledger/runledger-runtime/examples/producer_worker/worker.rs:51 prints worker ready before Supervisor::builder_from_env(...).build() at lines 53-55. README embeds it at line 296 and instructs users to wait for that text at line 359. The example may report ready before supervisor construction fails or any loop initializes. Native startup_observer already exists. Keep definition availability distinct from worker initialization; do not imply that the observer proves database health or durable processing. Source-confirmed, not newly executed against a startup-failure fixture.

fields.description: Audit of 7cc8c82e: JobProgressUpdate (types/lifecycle.rs:70-80), update_job_progress and update_job_progress_for_lease (queue/lifecycle/progress.rs:312-351) are deprecated since 0.11.0 but still exported through jobs and the prelude in 0.13.0. Unlike harmless aliases, the old input preserves arbitrary JobStage writes and funnels them into shared SQL. queue_running_progress.rs:323 explicitly tests setting a claimed job back to Scheduled; typed ordinary progress cannot express that. This compatibility branch preserves a known weaker lifecycle shape, and the prelude makes it easy for a new agent to adopt. Decide a staged public cut/compatibility quarantine after checking real downstream needs; do not alter historical database migrations. Inventory older 0.1.2/0.8/0.11 aliases separately and distinguish inert aliases from invariant-restoring shims.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Recorded compatibility decision and bounded retirement scope; new-consumer guidance/prelude no longer present stage-bearing progress as ordinary integration; hard-cut obligations met if removal approved; preserve supported running/ordinary progress behavior and failure tests.

Ranked actionable findings: (1) observer panic-payload destruction escapes Runlimit catch-and-ignore helpers, new batter-6p9u; (2) native worker examples only handle Ctrl-C, new batter-ad1e; (3) fail-open environment parsing/defaulting promoted by native quick start, existing batter-bwc7 with expanded propagation evidence; (4) deprecated stage-bearing progress remains in prelude and mutates arbitrary stages, new batter-hixn; (5) producer-worker example announces readiness before supervisor construction, new batter-f1j7.

Several older native aliases (since 0.1.2, 0.8, 0.11) merit a bounded inventory, prioritizing behavior-changing shims over inert aliases.

data.text: Codex review (gpt-6.2-astra, xhigh) of the uncommitted upgrade found, and source inspection confirmed: (1) SQLx 0.9.1 new_without_pgpass reads ambient PGHOSTADDR into hostaddr, which connect prefers over the URL host; batter-sqlx ConnectionPlan::resolve and runledger-test-support fixture URLs were redirectable. (2) #4375 re-send also covers simple-query raw_sql and reads only the SQLSTATE, so a statement with earlier non-transactional effects that raises 26000/0A000 repeats them outside a transaction (review reproduced on PG18). My earlier 'not a replay' note was wrong. (3) With statement cache disabled, persistent queries use the unnamed statement and the custom-type re-parse only runs for nonpersistent ones: first uncached enum query in a transaction fails 26000 (review reproduced on PG18). User chose upgrade + mitigate. Mitigation: new public batter_sqlx::test_support::AmbientHostAddress, resolution refuses when PGHOSTADDR is present (injectable lookup, offline unit test); Runledger shared fixture startup asserts PGHOSTADDR absent before any container (unit tests). (2) and (3) are disclosed in guarantees and the ecosystem upgrade record; Batter cannot disable them.

fields.description: Observed 2026-11-18 on macOS (aarch64), pinned Rust 1.100.0, during bash scripts/verify.sh workspace-tests: watchdog::tests::parent_unwind_kills_reaps_and_joins_capture_reader (crates/batter-core/tests/non_yielding/watchdog_tests.rs:102) failed with 'unwind cleanup took 5.005681584s; expected completion before 5s'. The bound deliberately includes child startup. The same target then passed 3/3 alone (cargo test -p batter-core --test non_yielding --locked). Found while verifying batter-c5ci, which does not touch batter-core. Do not relax the semantic bound without showing that the 5 s limit still distinguishes the 10 s child emergency exit; consider separating startup from the measured unwind interval.
fields.title: batter-core non_yielding parent_unwind_kills_reaps_and_joins_capture_reader flakes in the workspace matrix

data.text: Cause: watchdog_tests.rs measured the 5 s bounds from spawn (FixtureChild::started), so loaded-matrix child startup consumed the unwind/exit budget. First verify.sh rerun after the initial fix exposed the same class in parent_pipe_closure_ends_blocked_runtime_without_cleanup (watchdog kill at 5.001 s after runtime-drop-started; expected PARENT_GONE). Fix: parent_unwind times unwind from after fixture-entered (< EXIT_LIMIT) and separately asserts spawn-to-cleanup < EMERGENCY_LIMIT (child arms its emergency exit after spawn, so this exactly excludes waiting for exit 75). parent_pipe_closure waits EXIT_LIMIT from closure; exact code 74 still separates it from emergency 75. Mutation evidence (macOS aarch64, Rust 1.100.0): FixtureChild::drop changed to child.wait() -> parent_unwind fails 'unwind cleanup took 9.995s'; launch EOF exit replaced with park -> parent_pipe_closure fails with watchdog SIGKILL. Target passes 50/50 with both fixes.

fields.description: ADR-010 recurring-defect assessment from batter-c5ci. SQLx 0.9.1 (#4514, libpq semantics) applies ambient PGHOSTADDR to every PgConnectOptions URL parse that omits hostaddr, and offers no env-free constructor or hostaddr reset. Point guards in ConnectionPlan::resolve and Runledger shared startup were followed by a second review finding the same redirect at other sites: batter-sqlx and Runlimit live-test helpers (e.g. profile_privileges_live, runlimit test_pool), Runledger drop_database after startup and the delayed-startup test, FixtureScope/FixtureSuite template initializers, scripts/test_runledger_tools.py live CLI test, and the owned_pool/verification facade examples. About 71 URL-based connection sites in ~40 files. Cause: upstream protocol change plus a Batter design gap (no library-owned URL-to-options boundary). Candidate remedy: one public batter-sqlx constructor that refuses PGHOSTADDR (and documents the process-environment precondition), adopted by every internal site and example, plus a source-inventory test like crates/batter/tests/panic_hook_ownership.rs forbidding raw URL parsing/connect(url) outside it; Python children scrub PGHOSTADDR. Alternative: keep SQLx 0.9.0 and request an env-free constructor upstream. Public-contract change: needs user decision.
fields.title: Central PostgreSQL URL boundary that refuses ambient PGHOSTADDR under SQLx 0.9.1

data.text: Second Codex review (gpt-6.2-astra, xhigh, branch vs master) confirmed six findings: four PGHOSTADDR redirect sites beyond the two guards (live-test helpers, Runledger teardown/delayed-startup, template initializers, Python live CLI test, facade examples), plus published rustdoc still promising no automatic replay (lib.rs:275/362, pooled_query.rs:22, atomic_runner.rs:194; no_tx migrations run outside a transaction). ADR-010 recurrence trigger met; dependent PGHOSTADDR repairs paused pending user decision. Design scope split into a child Bead.

Source scan crates/batter/tests/postgres_endpoint_boundary.rs rejects PgConnection::connect, pool connect/connect_lazy with non-literal URL, from_str/from_url, typed parse; exemptions: runledger-tui and native examples (libpq semantics), TLS/TCP files, the scan itself; stale-exemption check. CI on 19c1c9a4 passed every job, including verify (1.100.0) 20m42s, Native Runlimit PostgreSQL and the macOS subprocess harness. Third Codex review (gpt-6.2-astra xhigh, full branch) confirmed 5 findings: inferred .parse() URL sites missed by the scan (profile_privileges_live x2, profile_login, postgres-lifecycle live.rs); SQLx 0.9.1 make_socket_path precedes hostaddr so a hostless or host=/dir URL with hostaddr uses a socket; scan missed PgPool::connect/connect_lazy; reference live_tests ? skipped awaited lease cleanup; examples misreported AmbientHostAddress as invalid URL. Fixed in the next commit within the accepted boundary design: HostAddressShadowedBySocket (batter-sqlx, runledger-test-support; Runlimit helper asserts), scan rules + fixtures, cleanup-path match, operator messages. ADR-010 recurrence assessment after Codex round 4 (gpt-6.2-astra xhigh, branch 71c8410f): 6 confirmed findings. (1) template initializers check only env PGHOSTADDR, not socket-shadowed URL hostaddr; (2) exempt native roots (runledger-tui, two native examples) diverge from libpq: PGHOST=/tmp + URL hostaddr connects to socket; (3) runledger-test-support with_database_name drops the admin URL query, so host/hostaddr endpoint params differ between admin and lease connections under 0.9.1; (4) refresh_runledger_sqlx: psql honours URL hostaddr but SQLx CLI uses the socket; (5) scan misses PgListener::connect(url) and runledger_postgres::DbPool alias; (6) literal connect_lazy exemption admits live URLs (40 literal sites). Classification: upstream protocol change (SQLx 0.9.1 hostaddr semantics: env, socket precedence, query handling) plus an enforcement design gap (text scan cannot resolve aliases/types). Point fixes cover more cases of the same protocol. Candidate remedy: boundary refuses hostaddr in env and URL everywhere (removes socket-shadow and derived-URL classes), and replace call-form text rules with clippy disallowed-methods (alias/type resolved), keeping text rules only for parse(); rewrite inert lazy placeholders. Alternatives: point-patch the six; or revert to SQLx 0.9.0. Paused for user decision.

User chose: refuse hostaddr everywhere + Clippy enforcement. Round 4 fixes (ce754aec): DeclaredHostAddress (any spelling) at all boundaries; template initializers validate URL via connect_options; runledger_postgres re-exports the boundary for runledger-tui and native examples (exemptions removed); derived Runledger fixture URLs keep query, drop dbname; refresh script refuses URL hostaddr; Clippy disallowed-methods in root/runledger/runlimit clippy.toml (Pool/PoolOptions connect/connect_lazy, Connection::connect, ConnectOptions::from_url, PgListener::connect) - flagged exactly the 39 placeholder pools, all rewritten. Round 5 (5613f94f, gpt-6.2-astra xhigh): 4 findings fixed - refresh redacts URL parse errors and refuses literal '#'; fault proxies refuse socket fixtures (regression from query preservation); scan catches qualified turbofish and multiline typed parse.
